headline: A real-click study finds a no-persona LLM ranker outperforms a synthetic persona panel
summary: A July 2026 paper tests whether a demographic persona panel improves LLM forecasts of real audience response. It compares a fixed ten-persona panel with a no-persona ranker on held-out Upworthy headline A/B tests. Because most tests had no statistically reliable winner, the primary analysis uses 399 of 1,695 packages. On that subset, the paper reports Kendall tau 0.361 and top-1 accuracy 49.2% for the no-persona baseline, versus 0.084 and 34.6% for the persona panel. The direction holds across three Upworthy splits and tested model tiers; the paper also reports a significant gpt-4.1 cross-family gap. A public repository contains scripts and aggregated artifacts for regenerating reported tables, while raw persona generations are withheld. Results concern aggregate ranking of historical English headlines, not all persona use or current marketing outcomes.
